rules: $earnings_per_share combined with a price or return term produced this round's top 3 fitnesses (7.94, 5.04, 3.17) — favor more fundamental x price/volume pairings over pure price/volume ones.

TS_MEAN($return,10) multiplied by a plain price/volume co-factor (high/close ratio, dollar-volume rank, close delta) failed the cheap screen 3 times this round; the same term paired with $earnings_per_share scored 7.94 and 3.17 — prefer a fundamental co-factor for this term over a price/volume one.

Un-ranked return-sum/delta factors over 40+ day windows with no cross-sectional or fundamental anchor made up over half this round's rejections and mostly failed the cheap screen outright (t 0.04-0.43) — wrap in CS_RANK or pair with a fundamental instead of proposing them bare.
TS_CORR($return, $volume, 42) gave this round's weakest signal (t=0.04) — deprioritize return/volume correlation at medium windows.

Multiplying a bounded price ratio by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, ...) caused 2 of 4 correlation rejections because dollar_volume dominates the product — rank or demean dollar_volume before combining rather than multiplying it in raw.

4 of 19 rejections were archived trees re-proposed with only a changed window constant or an added DELAY/extra-smoothing wrapper — when mutating an archived parent, change the operator or input field, not just the constants.

The fast/price_volume/low niche looks saturated: $close normalized by rolling std/min/max in the 15-63 day band produced this round's weakest accept (0.004, itself near-duplicate of a rejected subtree) plus 2 of 4 correlation rejections — shift search toward the mixed/medium and mixed/slow niches that produced this round's 4 best scores.

CS_DEMEAN'd asset_turnover crossed with a short close-delta, and CS_RANK of a $return win-count, both cleared the bar only modestly (1.85, 0.89) — iterate on these with alternate fundamentals or count windows rather than repeating plain price/volume normalizations.
